elements.texte:
[cheerful] To record the number of spots in each workshop, we add a spots column.

This column is added to the workshops table.

CREATE TABLE creates a new table.

Here, the workshops table already exists: to add a column to it while keeping its data, we use ALTER TABLE.

So we change it with ALTER TABLE, which changes the structure of an existing table.

ADD COLUMN adds a column, with its name and type.

Your turn!

With DEFAULT 12, the spots column holds 12 as soon as it’s added.

This applies to each of the five workshops already recorded.

Their titles, dates and coaches stay intact: no row is lost.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Your turn!

The phone number is information about the coach.

So we add it in a phone column of the coaches table.

The number is filled in only once per coach.

Each coach has their own number: so we don’t write a DEFAULT.

Your turn!

Without DEFAULT, existing rows get null: the cell stays empty.

A few days later, Karim records each coach’s number there.

He uses UPDATE for this, which changes values: you’ll learn it later on.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] To rename a column, we write RENAME COLUMN.

Your turn!

After RENAME COLUMN, we give the current name, sessions, then TO followed by the new name, sessions underscore left.

The values stay the same.

The column is now called sessions underscore left.

Each card keeps its number of sessions: 10, 5 and 8.

The CHECK constraint follows the new name: sessions underscore left greater than or equal to 0.

The same way, ALTER TABLE cards RENAME TO membership underscore cards would rename the table itself.

UPDATE changes the values while keeping the column.

In the next lesson, you’ll learn to remove a whole table.

You’ll do it with DROP TABLE: the table disappears with all its data.
